item.title: Cyclical high-magnitude lake drainage slows Greenland ice sheet motion
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79659-3

Four decades of satellite data show that repeated outburst floods from ice-marginal lakes beside a Greenland glacier reset its flow to a slow state for several years, acting as a natural brake on ice motion.

item.title: EcoVAE: a generative deep learning method for global species distribution prediction
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79791-0

Predicting where species live is key to protecting biodiversity. The authors present EcoVAE, a generative model that rapidly and accurately predicts global species distributions, reveals species associations, and identifies sampling gaps.

item.title: Retraction Note: Combination of PARP and KRAS<sup>G12D</sup> inhibitors enhances therapeutic efficacy by exploiting vulnerabilities in PDAC
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-80283-4

Retraction Note: Combination of PARP and KRASG12D inhibitors enhances therapeutic efficacy by exploiting vulnerabilities in PDAC

item.title: Subsets of regulatory T cells are CD1a-reactive and dysfunctional in psoriasis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79338-3

T regulatory cells (Treg) cells may be involved with the regulation of immune responses in psoriasis. Here, using psoriasis samples from humans, the authors characterize the function of CD1a-responsive Treg cells in psoriasis and show that these cells secrete IL-10 in response to lysophosphatidylcholine and are found in close proximity to CD1a+ antigen-presenting cells and are potentially dysfunctional in psoriasis.

item.title: Catalyst-free thermal dehydropolycondensation for precise synthesis of silicon-incorporated polythiophenes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79642-y

The synthesis of silicon-incorporated polythiophenes typically requires metal catalysts, which show poor polymerisation control and require post-synthesis purification. Here, the authors report a metal catalyst-free thermal dehydropolycondensation strategy for the synthesis of silicon-incorporated polythiophenes with well defined structures, narrow dispersities and high charge carrier mobilities.

item.title: Gut microbiota-derived phenylacetylglutamine exacerbates aortic aneurysm and dissection via activating macrophage integrin β1 in male mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79232-y

Here the authors report a link between the gut microbial metabolite PAGln and aortic aneurysm and dissection in patients and show that it worsens disease in mice by promoting inflammation in the aortic wall.

item.title: Host control of rhizobial proliferation in soybean nodules
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79800-2

Legumes must tightly regulate rhizobial proliferation to optimize symbiotic benefits and avoid pathogenicity. Here the authors show a role for cell wall derived demethylesterified pectin in constrains rhizobial growth in soybean nodules

item.title: Dissecting the root-fungal interface in 3D reveals spatially distinct signalling landscapes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79701-4

Plant-fungal interactions in the rhizosphere influence plant health. Here the authors describe an optically transparent granular microgel matrix that mimics the mechanical properties of natural microenvironments to dissect fungal development and pathogenesis.

item.title: Author Correction: A sensitive red/far-red photoswitch for controllable gene therapy in mouse models of metabolic diseases
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79407-7

Author Correction: A sensitive red/far-red photoswitch for controllable gene therapy in mouse models of metabolic diseases

item.title: De novo identification of protein domains in cryo-electron tomography maps from AlphaFold2 models
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79502-9

Identifying proteins in medium- to low-resolution cryo-electron tomography density maps remains challenging. Here the authors develop DomainSeeker, which combines AlphaFold2 models with experimental data to identify protein domains from density maps.

item.title: CD33-CD45 interaction in Alzheimer’s disease susceptibility
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79540-3

CD33 and CD45 are both genetically linked to Alzheimer’s risk. Here the authors show the two proteins physically interact, and this interaction is increased in Alzheimer’s disease.

item.title: A spectral-spatial interweaver for hyperdimensional photonic computing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78734-z

Photonic computing promises faster, more energy-efficient AI, but hardware scaling remains challenging. Here, the authors present HyperON, a TFLN-based hyperdimensional photonic computing network combining a spectral-spatial interweaver with wavelength-parallel modulators.

item.title: ORE1 stabilizes PIF4 protein through a UBP12/UBP13-dependent regulatory module in thermomorphogenesis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79802-0

Plants adapt their growth to warmth, but how aging signals tune protein stability remains unclear. Here, the authors show that the senescence factor ORE1 acts as a scaffold to stabilize the heat regulator PIF4 via UBP12/UBP13-mediated deubiquitination, driving warmth induced growth.

item.title: A conceptual analysis of One Health and Person-Centred Practice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79922-7

This Review examines how One Health and person-centred practice can strengthen each other. The authors argue that care should account for animal and ecosystem health, while One Health should attend to people’s lived experience.

item.title: Non Hermitian synthetic phase shifter with topologically protected phase control via tunable losses
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79534-1

Programmable photonic circuits typically rely on refractive-index modulation for active control, limiting scalability. Here, authors develop and validate a synthetic phase-shifter framework using optical loss modulation to achieve full-cycle phase control protected by topological quantities.

item.title: Biomass-based platform for pesticide management balancing field efficacy with postharvest residue via dynamic adhesion switch
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79321-y

Pesticide formulations must balance two competing requirements—robust adhesion during cultivation and efficient removal in postharvest. Here, the authors developed a thermoresponsive biomass-based dynamic adhesion switch and constructed a Pickering emulsion system loaded with the UV-sensitive pesticide emamectin benzoate.

item.title: Mesophase-induced vitrification in coordination polymers via aliphatic chain dynamics
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79687-z

Coordination-polymer glasses offer structural functionality and processability but are hindered by poor thermal stability and high melting points. Here, the authors report mesophase-induced vitrification in magnesium-based frameworks, enabling glass formation without melting while preserving network integrity and mechanical stiffness.

item.title: Quasi-degenerate cation occupation enables oxygen-vacancy defect healing in nonlinear optical crystals
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79746-5

A quasi-degenerate cation occupation strategy offers a pathway to overcome substitution-induced defects in functional crystals. Its validation in La3TiGa5O14 demonstrates effective oxygen-vacancy healing and improved nonlinear optical performance.

item.title: CARM1-mediated methylation controls interactions of ALIX with key partners important for cytokinesis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79275-1

ALIX methylation by CARM1 controls CD2AP levels at the midbody and is important for cytokinesis. Their findings reveal a role for protein arginine methylation in the last step of cell division.

item.title: Nationwide high-resolution assessment reveals the underestimated carbon sink of Chinese parks
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79932-5

Based on net primary productivity, the 8,137 parks across mainland China sequestered 52.7 Mt C in 2020. Within the 5,425 urban parks, large ones (>100 hectares) contributed over 90%, while 10-50 hectares ones drove the shift from carbon sources to sinks.

item.title: Intramolecular electrophilic aminations of indoles enable divergent bond migrations to access piperidinoindolines and δ-carbolines
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 23 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79515-4

C–C migration rearrangements of spiro[indole-3,3′-pyrrolidines] are well established, but their isomeric spiro[indole-3,2′ pyrrolidine] counterparts remain unexplored. Here, the authors report a versatile strategy enabling selective C–C or C–N migration to access piperidinoindolines and δ-carbolines, with promising antitumour activity.

item.title: Electrically induced glass transition of polyelectrolyte complexes enables kinetic ionic diodes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79559-6

The glass transition induces changes in material properties, transforming a rigid glass into a soft rubber. Here the authors demonstrate an electrically induced glass transition in a polyelectrolyte complex, sandwiched between two oppositely charged ionoelastomers and applying time-temperature-salt superposition principle.

item.title: The genetic and proteomic determinants of pediatric stature development and their link to adult height and type 2 diabetes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79465-x

Childhood growth reflects complex genetic and biological processes, but their developmental timing is not fully understood. Here, the authors identify stage‑specific genetic and proteomic influences on growth from infancy through childhood, and reveal links between early growth patterns and later type 2 diabetes risk.

item.title: A quantitative deep-learning-based framework reveals a continuum of chromatin sensitivities across transcription factors
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79404-w

The authors develop a deep-learning-based framework revealing that TF binding sensitivity to chromatin is a continuum rather than a binary feature, and that binding patterns can be explained by a mixture of hierarchical and cooperative mechanisms.

item.title: Benzoxaboroles target CPSF3 for degradation through a SUMO-dependent pathway in trypanosomes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79400-0

Benzoxaborole drugs, such as acoziborole, target CPSF3 and mRNA processing in multiple parasites. Here the authors find that these drugs rapidly and specifically target trypanosome CPSF3 for degradation, in a SUMO- and proteasome-dependent manner.

item.title: Foliar and floral frost damage reshape reproductive phenology with limited carry-over effects
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79723-y

Late spring frost can damage plant tissues and disrupt reproduction. The authors show that frost damage to leaves shortens the fruit development period, whereas damage to flowers prolongs it, with limited carry-over effects into the following year.

item.title: Chronically stable, frequency-selective auditory brainstem stimulation via ultra-flexible penetrating electrode arrays
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79747-4

Surface auditory brainstem implants have poor spatial resolution and limited tonotopic access. Here, the authors develop a high-density, ultra-flexible penetrating array for frequency-selective cochlear nucleus stimulation and use-dependent plasticity in downstream auditory circuits.

item.title: Desmin filaments extend along actin filaments within the mouse skeletal muscle sarcomere
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79344-5

Here, the authors use super-resolution microscopy to show that desmin filaments extend beyond Z-lines and align with actin inside mouse skeletal muscle sarcomeres, where they help support force generation when sarcomeres are stretched.

item.title: Denitrogenative glycosylations of glycosyl sulfonohydrazides
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79707-y

Despite notable progress, the development of novel and efficient glycosyl radical precursors that are readily accessible, synthetically versatile, and compatible with stereoselective coupling platforms remains an ongoing challenge. Here the authors report a nickel-catalysed stereoselective denitrogenative glycosylation of redox-neutral glycosyl sulfonohydrazides via anomeric C–N bond homolysis.

item.title: Accelerating high-throughput catalyst screening by direct generation of equilibrium adsorption structures
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79243-9

The authors develop DBCata, a generative model trained without energy or force labels to produce near-equilibrium adsorption structures, enabling faster screening of candidate catalysts.

item.title: Greenhouse gas responses to coastal wetland land use change vary by ecosystem and conversion pathway
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79685-1

This study shows that greenhouse gas responses to coastal wetland land use change depend on the original ecosystem and conversion pathway, highlighting the climate value of conserving vegetated wetlands and targeting restoration.

item.title: Entropy-engineered polar heterogeneity enables near-decoupled polarization–strain behavior for high-density energy storage
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79625-z

Strong polarization–strain coupling limits the energy density and reliability of lead-free dielectric capacitors. Here, the authors show that entropy-engineered polar heterogeneity weakens this coupling, enabling ultrahigh energy storage with minimal electrostrain.

item.title: Shape conforming Janus hydrogel for preventing anastomotic leaks
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79644-w

Anastomotic leaks remain a major complication of gastrointestinal surgery, yet existing sealants often fail to provide durable coverage of irregular tissue surfaces. Here, the authors develop a Janus powder-derived dressing composed of an adhesive porous layer mechanically interlocked with a non-adhesive backing. The material conforms to anastomotic tissues, resists unwanted post-surgical adhesions, and provides sustained sealing, offering a promising strategy for leak prevention and repair.

item.title: [c2]Daisy-chain molecular turing machines with switchable fluorescence outputs
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79590-7

Synthetic small-molecule machines capable of bidirectionally reading and writing information on molecular tapes with visual output remain elusive due to the challenge in amplifying molecular-scale motions into macroscopic signals. Here, the authors report two [c2]daisy-chain molecular Turing machines that convert mechanical motions into fluorescence signals.

item.title: Landscape fire sourced PM2.5, cause-specific paediatric hospitalisations, and the role of tree cover
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79586-3

Greater tree cover is associated with lower risks and burdens of landscape fire smoke-related hospitalisations in children and adolescents across seven countries and territories, suggesting potential benefits of expanding tree cover.

item.title: Plankton ecological complexity amplifies climate-driven weakening of the ocean biological pump
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79817-7

Using one Earth system model with increasingly complex plankton food webs, the study finds that greater ecological complexity amplifies climate-driven declines in ocean carbon export, suggesting simple models may underestimate future weakening.

item.title: Localized strain-engineered 1D electron guides in 2D MoS<sub>2</sub> devices with synaptic memory and high-mobility transistor functionalities
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79577-4

Local strain engineering can tune the electronic and transport properties of 2D semiconductors. Here, the authors report the realization of multifunctional strained 2D MoS2 devices on patterned HfO2 substrates, showing synaptic memory or high-mobility transistors functionalities depending on the carrier transport direction.

item.title: Mapping temperature using transmission Kikuchi diffraction
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77502-3

Measuring nanoscale temperatures is hard: contact probes perturb samples and optical methods lack resolution. Here, authors develop Kikuchi diffraction thermometry, a non-contact electron microscopy method that maps nanoscale temperatures via tiny heat-induced lattice changes.

item.title: A global atlas of digital dermatology to map innovation and disparities
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78602-w

The authors map 1.1 million dermatology images to assess the diversity of data used to train AI and find major gaps in darker skin tones and children, highlighting the importance of representation for future data collection.

item.title: Deep ultraviolet gallium-oxide avalanche photodiodes reaching an impulse-response-derived gain-bandwidth record of 152 GHz
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79355-2

Solar-blind gallium oxide photodetectors enable secure deep-ultraviolet communication but face a trade-off between speed and gain. Dong et al. engineered a multilayer avalanche device achieving nanosecond response, high gain, and a record gain-bandwidth product.

item.title: [Representative figure added] Depth-enhanced molecular imaging with two-photon oblique plane microscopy
item.description: Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

item.title: Chemical upcycling of mixed polyolefins via rapid C–H nitration
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79649-5

Post-polymerization modification provides a route to upcycle polyolefin waste, but most current systems have long reaction times and are substrate specific. Here, the authors report the rapid C-H nitration of various polyolefins with high selectivity and functionalisation degrees, forming functionalised polyolefins with enhanced tensile and adhesive properties.

item.title: Optical observation of ultrafast carrier separation in InGaN photocatalyst nanostructures
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79779-w

The authors show that ultrafast carrier separation causes the rapid photoluminescence decay in nanostructured InGaN photocatalysts from time resolved photoluminescence and differential reflectance spectroscopy supported by numerical modelling.

item.title: SMC5/6 safeguards chromatin compartments and TAD boundaries for genome stability
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79493-7

The SMC5/6 complex protects genome stability, but how it shapes 3D genome folding is unclear. Here, the authors show that SMC5/6 loss in human cells alters chromatin compartments and activates inflammatory and cancer-related genes, changes that are uncoupled from DNA damage.

item.title: Linking human sources to antibiotic resistance genes in global surface waters
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79418-4

In this study, the authors used measurement data combined with modeling and machine learning to estimate global human generation of five individual ARGs and intI1, discharge, and surface-water abundance, highlighting hotspots of per-capita generation and total abundance.

item.title: Double-membrane-spanning RNA export pores are a conserved feature in nidovirus replication organelles
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78986-9

This study shows that arteriviruses, like coronaviruses, form pore complexes that span their double-membrane replication organelles, pointing to a conserved nidovirus strategy that links the synthesis, export and packaging of viral RNA.

item.title: High-κ bismuth molybdate single-crystalline dielectric for high-temperature two-dimensional transistors
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79576-5

High temperature stability is an important requirement for future electronic circuits based on 2D semiconductors. Here, the authors report the synthesis of high-κ (54.2) Bi2MoO6 single-crystalline nanosheets and their application as gate dielectric for 2D MoS2 transistors, showing good thermal stability of the devices up to 500 K.

item.title: VHSeek: biology foundation model-based virus representations revealing virus host associations
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79392-x

The authors present VHSeek, a tool that uses DNA and protein sequence representations to predict viral hosts and prioritize candidate virus-host associations across large viral collections.

item.title: var2csa transcription implicates variant surface antigen switching in cerebral malaria pathogenesis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78682-8

In this study, the authors report case-control studies in Mali and Malawi showing that cerebral malaria is associated with increased transcription of var2csa and EPCR-ICAM1 dual binding PfEMP1s, rather than EPCR-binding variants alone suggesting that var gene regulation may be a driver of severe disease.

item.title: Laser ablation rapid evaporative ionisation mass spectrometry imaging with few-micrometer sampling pixels
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79489-3

In mass spectrometry imaging, smaller pixel sizes usually come at the cost of reduced signal and more complex sample preparation. Here, authors develop a gentle infrared laser ablation approach that maps metabolites and lipids at few-micron pixel sizes in fresh-frozen and clinical tissue in open air.

item.title: Wnk1 drives CD4+ T cell lineage fate determination and bone marrow homing in a mouse model of retinal autoimmune disease
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 20 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79609-z

CD4 T cells are central to the pathogenesis of uveitis and related inflammatory responses by promoting myeloid cell infiltration. Here, by leveraging scRNA-seq and a mouse model of experimental autoimmune uveitis, the authors identify the kinase Wnk1 as a key regulator of CD4 T cell differentiation, migration and metabolic reprogramming and as a coordinator of T cell-bone marrow crosstalk that contributes to myeloid-biased hematopoiesis.

item.title: Disturbance increases soil microbiome functional redundancy but decreases capacity for insurance via winnowed environmental responsiveness
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79487-5

More redundancy doesn’t always mean more resilience. Here, the authors use seven-year-long metagenomics data from soils above Centralia’s coal seam fire to show that heat disturbance increases microbial functional redundancy but narrows environmental responsiveness, potentially lowering insurance against future stress.

item.title: Bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes as saturated bioisosteres of meta-benzene
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79402-y

The authors synthesize bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes and provide support for their ability to mimic meta-substituted benzenes in biological contexts.

item.title: Automated data to model transformation for constraint programming with AI
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78715-2

The authors introduce CPAM-LLM, a framework that converts unstructured optimization problems into executable constraint models using LLMs, retrieval-augmented generation, data augmentation, and dynamic constraints.

item.title: In vivo programming of dual-targeted CAR-T cells facilitates vascular disruption and T-cell infiltration in solid tumors
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79342-7

Li and colleagues introduce an mRNA lipid nanoparticle platform for the selective transfection of endogenous T cells within the spleen; by dual-targeted CAR T cell in vivo programming, the authors show that VEGFR2 CAR-T cells disrupt the tumor vasculature, favoring the infiltration and activity of tumor-directed CAR-T cells.

item.title: Modulating FCC/HCP phase boundaries in inverse Co@BO<sub>x</sub> catalysts via crystal-phase-ratio variation for propane oxidative dehydrogenation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79394-9

Oxidative dehydrogenation of propane (ODHP) offers a promising route to propylene, but developing catalysts that operate efficiently at low temperatures while maintaining high activity and selectivity remains a formidable challenge. Here, the authors report a Co@BOx inverse catalyst in which phase boundaries within the subsurface cobalt promoter enable efficient low-temperature ODHP.

item.title: Facial photographs reveal mortality risk beyond triage and clinical risk scores
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79581-8

Using 27,660 smartphone facial photos, researchers showed that the facial appearance from emergency admission predicts mortality and high-risk patients better than triage, early warning scores, vitals, or lab tests.

item.title: A dual-anchoring mechanism for hemimethylated CG-guided histone ubiquitylation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79633-z

VIM proteins regulate maintenance of plant CG methylation. Here the authors show how the interaction of VIM1 with hemimethylated linker DNA and the acidic patch of a nucleosome governs its histone ubiquitylation activity for maintenance of DNA methylation.

item.title: Protecting-group-lean platform for synthesizing diverse phenylethanoid glycosides uncovers antifibrotic leads
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79652-w

Phenylethanoid glycosides constitute one of the most structurally diverse classes of natural glycosides, yet systematic investigation is constrained by limited access to preparative quantities. Here, the authors report a protecting group-lean platform that delivers a 29-member library of phenylethanoid glycosides.

item.title: Interfacial mechanisms of gas-bubble friction
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79472-y

Zhang et al. report the interfacial mechanisms governing bubble friction on solids, demonstrating how surface structure, chemistry, and gas identity regulate bubble mobility. These insights advance friction tunable interfaces in bubble transport.

item.title: Designing 3D oxygen–diffusion scaffolds for high-performance metal fuels
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79710-3

This work develops a Ce-assisted strategy to build 3D oxygen-diffusion scaffolds in Al fuels, overcoming Al2O3 diffusion barriers and achieving complete oxidation and enhanced combustion.

item.title: Atomically ordered few-layer molybdenum boride MBenes for enhanced electromagnetic response
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 19 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79512-7

The authors develop a theory-guided molten-salt route that selectively removes aluminum to produce atomically ordered, few-layer MoB MBenes with few Mo vacancies. The preserved Mo−B framework enhances polarization and electromagnetic response.

item.title: Lysine-R2HGylation-C5 identified as a post-translational modification in R2HG-elevated cancers
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79668-2

R-2-hydroxyglutarate is a cancer-linked metabolite whose mechanisms are incompletely understood. Here, the authors identify and structurally characterize lysineR2HGylation as a protein modification and develop probes that reveal GSTP1 as a functional target in leukemia cells.

item.title: Low-temperature operation of Ag—C based anodeless all-solid-state pouch cells
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79291-1

Initially anode-free all-solid-state batteries with Ag-C interlayers promise high energy density but degrade in the cold. Here, authors identify suppressed Li-Ag alloying as the failure mechanism and introduce an activation protocol enabling durable cold cycling of pouch cells without material redesign.

item.title: A revised genome annotation of the model cyanobacterium Synechocystis based on start and stop codon-enriched ribosome profiling and proteogenomics
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79174-5

Information on protein-coding segments in a genome is frequently incomplete and genes encoding very short proteins are often overlooked. Here, the authors present a riboproteogenomic approach. The results support the existence of many additional protein-coding sequences in a model cyanobacterium.

item.title: Impact of Comorbid Depression and Anxiety on the Mortality among Adults with Cardiometabolic Diseases
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79803-z

Cardiometabolic diseases often coexist with depression or anxiety, but their prognostic implications remain unclear. Here, the authors show that depression/anxiety after cardiometabolic disease onset is associated with higher mortality, with variation by socioeconomic status.

item.title: VapC40 diverts autophagic flux from xenophagy to mitophagy via ammonia-dependent metabolic toxicity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79313-y

In this work, the authors show that a bacterial virulence factor from Mycobacterium bovis rewires nitrogen metabolism in infected immune cells, producing ammonia that damages lysosomes and mitochondria and allows the bacteria to avoid destruction.

item.title: Boosting Sensitivity of High-Dimensional Solid-State NMR of Proteins by Optimizing Coherence Transfers
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79563-w

The authors show that for complex state-of-the art solid-state NMR experiments on proteins, custom-designed pulses can strongly facilitate data acquisition, with important implications in the study of larger proteins.

item.title: Superionicity and premelting of iron-rich (Fe,Mg)O at Earth’s core-mantle boundary
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79523-4

Zhang et al. find that oxygen moves rapidly through iron-rich oxides near melting, lowering viscosity and enhancing element transport at Earth’s core-mantle boundary, with implications for ultralow-velocity zones.

item.title: An ingestible, bio-inspired self-powered electrocapsule for in situ ethanol clearance mitigates systemic and neurobehavioral toxicity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79347-2

Alcohol intoxication remains a leading cause of death and accidents. Here, the authors develop a self-powered electrocapsule that enables local intestinal ethanol conversion, reducing systemic ethanol exposure and associated toxicity in rats.

item.title: Encoding atomic-layer thickness via spin-dependent optical differentiation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78379-y

The determination of atomic-layer thickness is essential for both fundamental studies and device applications based on 2D materials. Here, the authors report an optical differentiation approach exploiting the spin Hall effect of light that enables a single-shot readout of the film thickness without spectrometers, scanning probes, or computational post-processing.

item.title: A master gene for Drosophila male courtship prevents the behavior in females via a truncated protein
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79460-2

The fruitless gene has long been thought to function only in male flies to control male courtship. Peng et al. identify a transiently expressed, truncated Fruitless protein in females that suppresses male-typical courtship behaviour.

item.title: Selective mTOR inhibition via FLCN drives TFE3-dependent VLDL-TG secretion and protects from MAFLD/MASH
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79397-6

The study identified a pathway that coordinates VLDL assembly and secretion regulated by non-canonical mTOR signaling. Targeting the pathway efficiently suppresses liver steatosis.

item.title: Supervised deep learning for efficient cryo-EM image alignment in drug discovery with cryoPARES
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78403-1

Cryo-electron microscopy studies often generate multiple datasets of closely related samples. Here, the authors present cryoPARES, a supervised deep-learning framework that reuses prior alignments to rapidly determine particle poses.

item.title: LRRK2-mediated phosphorylation of exocytic RABs disrupts neurotrophin/neuropeptide secretion
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77820-6

This study reveals that distinct RAB proteins control neuropeptide release in different neuron types and identifies LRRK2-mediated inhibition of RAB recruitment as a mechanism that may contribute to Parkinson’s disease-related neurodegeneration.

item.title: Author Correction: A preoperative Artificial Intelligence model to estimate cancer-specific mortality in nonmetastatic kidney cancer patients
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79624-0

Author Correction: A preoperative Artificial Intelligence model to estimate cancer-specific mortality in nonmetastatic kidney cancer patients

item.title: Author Correction: Modular assembly of an artificially concise biocatalytic cascade for the manufacture of phenethylisoquinoline alkaloids
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79702-3

Author Correction: Modular assembly of an artificially concise biocatalytic cascade for the manufacture of phenethylisoquinoline alkaloids

item.title: EpiPack: A computational framework for reference mapping and out-of-reference detection for single-cell ATAC-seq data with heterogeneous peak features
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78924-9

EpiPack maps single-cell chromatin accessibility data across heterogeneous datasets and identifies cell types and states absent from reference atlases, enabling analysis of disease-associated cellular changes.

item.title: RSM01, an extended half-life RSV monoclonal antibody with a high barrier to in vitro resistance
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79029-z

RSM01 showed broad neutralizing activity against circulating LMIC RSV strains. Authors found a high barrier to resistance, supporting RSM01 as an alternative should resistance emerge with widespread use of current licensed anti-RSV mAbs.

item.title: Dearomatization and cycloaddition of furans and indoles enable divergent syntheses of spirooxindole alkaloids
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79458-w

Dearomatization offers powerful routes to molecular complexity, yet strategies that couple distinct dearomatization products remain underdeveloped. Here, the authors report an oxidative strategy linking indole and furan dearomatization to rapidly access diverse tetracyclic spirooxindoles, including natural products.

item.title: Upcycling of polyolefin and polyester mixtures via a single-atom alloy
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79689-x

Mixed plastic waste is difficult to recycle because different polymers require separate processing. This study develops a catalyst that converts mixed plastics directly into fuel-range hydrocarbons with high liquid yield.

item.title: Transforming spinel LiMn<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> into a Na-layered cathode
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79390-z

Spinel LiMn2O4 has potential to be transformed into a layered Na-storage material, but the mechanism remains unclear. Here, authors investigate the ion migration mechanism during the transformation and evaluate the Na storage performance of the resulting material, including application in pouch and cylindrical cells.

item.title: Hydroxyl-mediated oxygen anchoring steers CO electroreduction toward ethanol
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79510-9

Converting carbon monoxide into ethanol is hindered by oxygen removing pathways. Here, the authors report a strontium-modified copper catalyst designed to organize surface hydroxyl groups, promoting oxygen retention and ethanol formation at industrially relevant current densities.

item.title: Brønsted/Lewis acid-catalyzed divergent cascade cyclization of alkoxyallene for the total synthesis of eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79505-6

Eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids are biogenetically related yet structurally distinct polycyclic monoterpenoids, whose syntheses have traditionally proceeded separately. Here, the authors report a divergent cascade from a common alkoxyallene precursor, enabling access to both scaffolds through acid controlled tandem pathways and total syntheses of representative alkaloids.

item.title: Author Correction: Adenine base editing-mediated exon skipping restores dystrophin in humanized Duchenne mouse model
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79730-z

Author Correction: Adenine base editing-mediated exon skipping restores dystrophin in humanized Duchenne mouse model

item.title: Knowledge-guided machine learning deciphers spatiotemporal dynamics in chemical reactor systems
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79078-4

A physics-informed neural network embeds coking and heat transfer knowledge via an output integration layer and region-weighted loss to predict reactor spatiotemporal fields; it matches conventional simulation results, improves peak wall temperature accuracy, and runs about five orders of magnitude faster than conventional simulations.

item.title: Improving molecular property prediction with score-based diffusion models
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79240-y

This work introduces a diffusion-based approach for small molecule prediction across a range of structure-activity and ADME tasks. It demonstrates strong predictive calibration and support for ensemble-driven uncertainty ranking.

item.title: Structurally guided wavefront neural encoder for broad-range generalizable 3D holography
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79408-6

A single AI hologram generator works across distances and color without retraining, by learning how light scales — a step towards versatile, adaptive 3D holographic displays.

item.title: Leveraging sequence purification for accurate prediction of multiple conformational states with AlphaFold2
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79677-1

Proteins often adopt distinct conformations to carry out their functions. Here, the authors introduce AF-ClaSeq, a method that improves multistate structure prediction by clarifying evolutionary signals.

item.title: Author Correction: Vulnerability to climate-driven pathogen-specific diarrheal diseases: secondary analysis from the Global Enteric Multicenter Study and Vaccine Impact on Diarrhea in Africa follow-up
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79111-6

Author Correction: Vulnerability to climate-driven pathogen-specific diarrheal diseases: secondary analysis from the Global Enteric Multicenter Study and Vaccine Impact on Diarrhea in Africa follow-up

item.title: Author Correction: Androgens drive SLC1A5-dependent metabolic reprogramming in polycystic ovary syndrome
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79406-8

Author Correction: Androgens drive SLC1A5-dependent metabolic reprogramming in polycystic ovary syndrome

item.title: Phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover enables rate-matched nitrate-sulfate paired electrolysis for ammonium persulfate synthesis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79620-4

Electrochemical conversion of nitrate-rich wastewater to valuable ammonium salts is promising. We report a phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover mechanism that synchronizes nitrate-reduction and sulfate-oxidation kinetics, enabling direct electrosynthesis of ammonium persulfate.

item.title: Directly visualizing the energy level structure of quantum dot molecules
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79672-6

Characterizing the energy spectrum of semiconductor quantum dots is essential for spin qubit operation but remains challenging across broad parameter ranges. Here, the authors use molecular spectroscopy to map one and two electron energy levels in a silicon double quantum dot as functions of detuning, tunnel coupling, and magnetic field.

item.title: Cytotoxic drugs and bispecific T cell engagers synergize to rewire host immunity and elicit polyclonal antitumor T cell responses
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79192-3

TAA×CD28 costimulatory bispecific antibodies are a class of immunotherapeutics that provide tumor-targeted CD28 costimulation to T cells by crosslinking CD28 on T cells to a tumor-associated antigen (TAA) expressed on tumor cells. Here, the authors show that cytotoxic therapies reprogram the tumor microenvironment and augment the antitumor immunity induced by TAA×CD28 bispecifics.

item.title: Assembly of a renal countercurrent system in a beetle
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79593-4

Developmental assembly of a powerful water conservation countercurrent exchange system in a beetle is orchestrated through dynamic crosstalk between its multiple constituent organs mediated by just two fibroblast growth factor signalling pathways.

item.title: Facet-dependent anion adsorption for electrolyte-Cu interfacial stability in initially anode-free Li-metal batteries
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79429-1

Initially anode-free lithium-metal batteries are limited by unstable interfacial reactions at Cu current collectors. Here, authors show that preferential anion adsorption can stabilize the copper interface and improve long-term cycling.

item.title: Site-specific N-glycoproteomic analysis of extracellular vesicles from seminal plasma reveals the molecular typing of azoospermia
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79570-x

This study presents EVGlyco, a low-input platform for site-specific N-glycoproteomic analysis of biofluid EVs. It identifies site-specific N-glycan signatures in seminal plasma EVs that distinguish azoospermia types and nonobstructive subtypes.

item.title: Chromatin priming of skeletal stem and progenitor cells governs cell fate during bone repair
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79160-x

Skeletal stem/progenitor cells in bone and skeletal muscle are diverse populations with distinct roles in bone repair. This study defines their transcriptomic and chromatin-priming signatures that control cell fate during regeneration.

item.title: Mapping dynamics of subcellular RNA and protein localization and organization using optimal transport
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79450-4

The authors introduce a computational tool SLOT to map mRNA and protein localization within cells, providing a framework and spatial atlas for studying molecular organization during early development and informing virtual cell models.

item.title: Chirality-locked low-dimensional bound states in the continuum lasers
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79359-y

Bound states in the continuum are intrinsically delocalized. Here, the authors realize localized bound state-in-the-continuum lasers at one-dimensional interfaces and zero-dimensional junctions by interfacing domains of opposite chirality.

item.title: Field-angle-resolved heat transport in UTe<sub>2</sub>: determination of nodal positions in the superconducting order parameter
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78019-5

Determining the gap symmetry of superconducting phases in UTe2 remains a central challenge. Here, the authors use field-angle-dependent thermal conductivity and theoretical analysis to identify b-axis point nodes in the low-field state, consistent with a B2u order parameter.

item.title: Emergent mesoscale nanoparticle patterns from a non-equilibrium liquid lens
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79569-4

Nanoparticle assembly at fluid interfaces is often viewed as unpredictable and dominated by uncontrolled non-equilibrium effects. Here, the authors show that evaporation-driven nanoparticle assembly reveals predictable morphologies through multiscale modeling, linking transport dynamics and kinetic arrest.

item.title: DPI-score: a deep learning-based metric for assessing protein-protein interfaces in cryoEM derived assemblies
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79090-8

The study introduces deep learning-based protein-protein interfaces’ quality score- DPI-score, that uses only structural coordinates, without engineered interface features. It provides complementary validation and detects errors at interfaces.

item.title: Tuning methanol-CO selectivity in CO<sub>2</sub> hydrogenation by Ga coordination engineering in ZnGa<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub>
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79788-9

Controlling whether carbon dioxide hydrogenation yields methanol or carbon monoxide remains challenging. This study shows that tuning gallium coordination in ZnGa₂O₄ directs distinct reaction pathways and product selectivity.

item.title: A subspecialty diagnostic system powered by self-supervised learning for cervical histopathology
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79121-4

Foundation models could be promising for cervical cancer screening, but have important limitations for their clinical deployment. Here, the authors introduce the Cervical Subspecialty Pathology (CerS-Path) diagnostic system, a self-supervised learning framework for cervical cancer pathology that outperforms state-of-the-art foundation models across multiple diagnostic tasks.

item.title: A Miniaturized Electrostatic Field Sensor Based on MOS Depletion-Layer Capacitance Modulation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79482-w

Static and low-frequency electric fields are important in power systems and insulating materials, but compact non-perturbing sensors remain challenging to build. Here, the authors show a miniaturized MOS-capacitance sensor that measures electric fields with high linearity and enables monitoring of surface charge and device electric fields.

item.title: Enhancer-driven gene regulatory network of human forebrain development provides insights into autism
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79602-6

The authors construct a gene regulatory network showing the potential role of specific enhancer elements in driving lineage imbalance in autism, explaining why forebrain organoids from autism probands show heterogeneity in the generation of excitatory neurons.

item.title: Boosting reinforcement learning for critical node detection with multi-topology training strategies
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78707-2

Critical node detection helps identify network elements whose removal most disrupts connectivity. Here, the authors develop a reinforcement-learning approach that trains on diverse graph topologies to improve generalization to both synthetic and real networks.

item.title: Geophysical conditions favoring precursory slip before major earthquakes
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79533-2

Laboratory experiments show that precursory slow slip before earthquakes is controlled by faultroughness and stress. On smooth faults, it is most pronounced at low stress, explaining whysmooth, fluid-rich megathrust faults often host precursors.

item.title: TRIM47 drives cardiac ischemia/reperfusion injury by impairing mitochondrial function and fatty acid metabolism in male mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79182-5

Cardiac I/R injury is a prevalent and intractable clinical complication. Here, the authors show that TRIM47 facilitates ubiquitination-dependent nuclear translocation of FOXO1 and the subsequent inhibition of HNF4α, thereby aggravating mitochondrial dysfunction, FAO defects and cardiac I/R injury.

item.title: Multi-ancestry genetic analysis reveals 29 novel rheumatoid arthritis loci, effector genes and drug repurposing opportunities
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79357-0

Integrated genetic, functional, and network-level analyses reveal how population-specific and shared genetic signals contribute to rheumatoid arthritis and provide new insights into disease mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities.

item.title: Photonic-assisted ingenious agile non-periodic oscillator (PIANO)
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79422-8

The study presents PIANO, a microwave photonic oscillator that generates frequency-agile microwave signals with rapid switching and ultra-low phase noise, while overcoming the cavity-delay constraint of conventional delay-based oscillators.

item.title: Room-temperature continuous-wave lasing-like emission from solution-processed bulk monolayer MoS<sub>2</sub> thin films
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79012-8

Scaling up atomically thin light emitters remains challenging. Here, authors develop solution-processable bulk-monolayer MoS2 films that preserve monolayer optical properties and exhibit room-temperature lasing-like emission under continuous optical pumping at just a few nW.

item.title: Signatures of a Kondo insulator in a multilayer moiré Superlattice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78687-3

Kondo insulator phases are traditionally found in materials with f-electrons. Here, the authors present evidence towards the realization of a tunable Kondo insulator in a monolayer WS2/bilayer WSe2 moiré superlattice.

item.title: Vagal afferent activation induces a dissociated NREM sleep-like state with wake-related locus coeruleus activity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79135-y

The role of peripheral signals in sleep state regulation is not well understood. Here authors show that vagal sensory afferent activation induces a NREMS-like state with low-frequency EEG, slowed heart rate, and cooling, while elevating locus coeruleus noradrenergic activity, revealing brain arousal within a sleep-like state.

item.title: Author Correction: The conformation-selective PI3Kδ inhibitor roginolisib in patients with advanced or metastatic cancer, including metastatic uveal melanoma: first-in-human clinical trial
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79579-2

Author Correction: The conformation-selective PI3Kδ inhibitor roginolisib in patients with advanced or metastatic cancer, including metastatic uveal melanoma: first-in-human clinical trial

item.title: The posterior paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus to nucleus accumbens medial shell circuit mediates an anti-pruritic response
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78362-7

Neural mechanisms underlying itch are not fully understood. Here authors show that the pPVT-NAcMed (posterior paraventricular nucleus of the thalamus to nucleus accumbens medial shell) circuit oppositely responds to histamine-dependent vs -independent itch, with LH inputs buffering the former, but chronic itch reduces postsynaptic efficacy, promoting sensitization and revealing differential processing.

item.title: Thermodynamic-guided tailoring of single-atom coordination environments via oxygen chemical potential for efficient C-N coupling
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79091-7

Precise control of single-atom coordination is hindered by thermodynamic and kinetic constraints. Here, the authors report tuning Fe-O coordination on CoWO4 via oxygen chemical potential control. Optimal Fe1O4 boosts hexamethylenetetramine electrosynthesis with high yield, efficiency and stability.

item.title: Post-pandemic immunity debt and environmental decoupling reshape urban influenza transmission
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79600-8

Using 1.88 million clinical records from Macau and regional and global surveillance, in this study, the authors show how reduced population immunity and renewed travel reshaped post-pandemic influenza transmission and weakened its usual links with climate.

item.title: Author Correction: Direct binding of CEP85 to STIL ensures robust PLK4 activation and efficient centriole assembly
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79190-5

Author Correction: Direct binding of CEP85 to STIL ensures robust PLK4 activation and efficient centriole assembly

item.title: Power-sensitive partnerships for just nature-based solutions in urban informal settlements
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79301-2

Nature-based solutions should better redistribute benefits and reduce climate risks for vulnerable groups in urban informal settlements. To enable this, we argue for power-sensitive partnerships and a deep commitment to pluralism in values, ways of knowing, and understandings of nature.

item.title: Selective aromatization of polyolefins by temporal decoupling from cracking
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79441-5

Turning plastic waste into useful chemicals is limited because breaking polymer chains and controlling products need conflicting conditions. This study separates these steps in time, enabling fast, durable aromatic production with lower emissions.

item.title: Depth-enhanced molecular imaging with two-photon oblique plane microscopy
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 13 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78668-6

Two-photon oblique plane microscopy combines high-numerical-aperture single-objective detection with two-photon light-sheet illumination, resolving subcellular and single-molecule dynamics deep in multicellular systems through standard glass-based mounting.

item.title: Scaling medical imaging report generation with multimodal reinforcement learning
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78767-4

Researchers developed UniRG, a reinforcement learning framework that optimizes clinically aligned composite rewards for medical imaging report generation. UniRG outperforms prior models and demonstrates strong generalization across unseen hospitals and datasets

item.title: Autapse-inspired neuromorphic hardware with synapse–neuron integration for bidirectional feedback control
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79401-z

Inspired by autapses in the nervous system, researchers integrated artificial synapses and neurons to enhance or suppress signals through self-feedback, opening a new path toward autonomous, self-regulating hardware.

item.title: Thin-film lithium niobate waveguide-integrated p-i-n Tungsten selenide photodiodes with 10Gbit/s data reception
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79595-2

Thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) is a promising photonic platform, but its integration with 2D materials remains challenging. Here, the authors report the realization of TFLN-based waveguide-integrated WSe2 photodetectors, showing a 3-dB bandwidth up to 1.12 GHz, up to 10 Gbit/s data rates and responsivity up to 492 mA/W in the visible range.

item.title: Structural basis of ligand-mediated transition to higher-order rubisco assemblies
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79451-3

Proteins often assemble into complexes, and while binding partners typically drive this, ligand binding can too. Here the authors show ligand binding drives distinct rubisco assemblies, revealing an evolutionary path to greater structural complexity.

item.title: Latitude modulates climate-driven maize yield gains across the central U.S. “warming hole”
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79428-2

Climate change affects crop yield variation across regions and seasons. This study suggests that climate impacts on maize yields shift from losses in the southern U.S. Corn Belt to gains in the north, driven by climate trends, thermal matching, and hybrid selection.

item.title: Evolution of the molybdenum and vanadium cycles through time and their impact on ancient nitrogen fixation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79171-8

Partitioning experiments and Fe-rich sediments show V was removed from Archean– Paleoproterozoic seawater more efficiently than Mo, enriching seawater in Mo relative to V and helping explain the early evolution of Mo-based nitrogenase.

item.title: A prefrontal microcircuit computes trial-wise discount of reinforcement during threat learning in male mice
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79254-6

Neural mechanisms underlying threat learning are not fully understood. Here authors identify a prefrontal circuit that constrains early threat learning in male mice. Local inhibitory neurons may release this constraint, providing a mechanism for regulating how strongly each experience shapes memory.

item.title: Phylogeographic and functional assembly of population-level bacterial immunity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79636-w

In this study, the authors use comparative genomics and cross-infection assays to show a spatially and evolutionarily structured bacterial immune reservoir in which interactions among defense systems can reinforce or undermine phage resistance, refining the pan-immunity framework.

item.title: A single NLS directs AGO1 import shaping small RNA loading and silencing outputs in Arabidopsis
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79175-4

Small RNAs guide ARGONAUTE proteins to their targets. Here the authors identify a pathway controlling AGO1 nuclear import and show that AGO1 subcellular localization shapes small RNA loading and silencing outputs in plants.

item.title: Constructing exclusive Pt@WOx interfacial sites enables selective C–O bond activation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79789-8

Precisely constructing metal–oxide catalysts with exclusively interfacial active sites remains challenging. Here, glycerol is selectively converted to 1,3-propanediol over catalysts in which Pt exists solely as isolated Pt@WOx interfacial sites.

item.title: Topographical mismatch sustains open microchannels in living soft tissue for non-destructive protein biopsy
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78755-8

Skin-attached devices can easily inflame or collapse. Here, the authors show a multi-lobed microneedle device that holds micron-scale conduits open for seven days, allowing repeated protein sampling from interstitial fluid

item.title: Single photon reflection from a quantum dot in a waveguide
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78984-x

The authors achieve efficient mode matching to a quantum-dot nanowire waveguide and demonstrate coherent single-photon reflection with strong antibunching, realizing a waveguide-QED quantum mirror.

item.title: Frequency-tagged fMRI reveals dual mechanisms of attentional enhancement and suppression
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79329-4

Rafeh et al. use frequency-tagged fMRI to demonstrate that selective attention relies on dual, independent neural mechanisms for target enhancement and surround suppression, elaborating on traditional unitary models of human visual attention.

item.title: Functionally divergent RHOA mutations drive peripheral T cell lymphoma development by engaging a common neomorphic pathway
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79260-8

RHOA mutation variants, exerting opposite effects on canonical RHOA signaling, are associated with peripheral T-cell lymphomas (PTCL). Here, the authors show that different RHOA mutants share a neomorphic activity that activates the transcription factor NFAT to drive PTCL.

item.title: UMIche: a UMI-centric analysis platform for enhancing molecular quantification accuracy in bulk and single-cell sequencing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79336-5

Errors in unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) can distort molecule counts. Here, the authors present UMIche, a platform for benchmarking deduplication methods, and show that set cover and majority voting are more robust as barcode errors increase.

item.title: Toward triggered generation of indistinguishable single photons from MoTe<sub>2</sub> quantum emitters
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78808-y

Two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides are promising single-photon platforms but achieving photon indistinguishability remains challenging. Here, the authors realize reproducible near-infrared quantum emitters in bilayer MoTe2 with high purity, electrical tunability, and record indistinguishability.

item.title: OsCPK17- and OsMPK6-mediated dual phosphorylation of OsPUB12 maintains OsPUB2-regulated OsPUB12 homeostasis and balances rice immunity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79063-x

OsPUB2 degrades OsPUB12 to promote rice immunity. Phosphorylation of OsPUB12 by OsCPK17 and OsMPK6 at two sites fine-tunes its stability and the plant’s defense response.

item.title: Low-thermal-budget solution-processed montmorillonite dielectric for low-voltage 2D electronics
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79139-8

The low temperature synthesis of high-quality dielectrics is desired for the development of 2D electronics. Here, the authors report an environmentally friendly synthesis method of solution-processed montmorillonite dielectric layers and their application for low-voltage 2D transistors and logic circuits.

item.title: Switchable nucleophile-electrophile chemistry enables functional four-electron Li-I<sub>2</sub> batteries
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79413-9

Iodine multi-electron conversion is crucial for high-performance Li-I2 batteries. Here, authors introduce a polarity switchable phthalimide that promotes I − /I0/I⁺ redox via tunable Lewis acid/base interactions, enabling flexible cells with high capacity and good cycling stability.

item.title: Nudix protein D250R promotes African swine fever virus infection by disrupting host ubiquitination machinery
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79340-9

This study uncovers a novel African swine fever virus (ASFV) immune-evasion mechanism targeting ubiquitin activation and identifies D250R as a key virulence factor. Loss of D250R attenuates the virus and supports its potential as a live attenuated vaccine candidate against ASF.

item.title: Geometrically and chemically dual-adaptive COFs for selective recognition of multiple uranium species in complex waters
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79383-y

Uranium recovery is hindered by the chemical complexity of uranium ions in natural waters. Here the authors report a geometrically and chemically dual-adaptive three-dimensional covalent organic framework which enables rapid and selective uranium-extraction across diverse aqueous chemistries.

item.title: A lactate-fatty acid loop drives prostate cancer bone colonization by mediating metabolic interplay between tumor cells and osteoblasts
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79651-x

Bone metastases in advanced prostate cancer remain difficult to treat and are associated with poor outcomes. Here, the authors show that bone-colonizing prostate tumor cells exploit lactate uptake via MCT1 to fuel tumor growth and promote osteogenesis, identifying MCT1 inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy.

item.title: The representational geometry of cognitive maps under cognitive control
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77621-x

The brain organizes relationships between entities into cognitive maps. Here, the authors show that complementary stable and context-dependent representational geometries balance stability and behavioral flexibility, with their geometry shaped by cognitive control.

item.title: Toward personalized deep brain stimulation via white matter stimulation and microstructure in depression
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79289-9

A study of 51 patients receiving deep brain stimulation for treatment-resistant depression shows that individual white matter stimulation and integrity jointly influence antidepressant response, supporting more personalized neuromodulation strategies.

item.title: High-entropy alloy aerogels promote selective glycerol oxidation to tartronate at industrial current densities
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78330-1

The production of tartronate from glycerol electrooxidation is limited by low selectivity at industrial-scale current densities. Here, the authors report a PtCuCoCeSn high-entropy alloy aerogel for regulated glycerol adsorption, enabling 81.4% selectivity and stable operation up to 240 hours.

item.title: Global environmental genomics reveals vast uncultivated protist diversity and taxonomic blind spots
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78712-5

In this study, the authors analyze over 30,000 assembled metagenomes across ecosystems to uncover hidden protist diversity, including major novel uncultivated lineages, and reveal their habitats and connections to other microbes.

item.title: A national baseline for methane sink habitats and methanotroph diversity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79316-9

In this study, the authors use metagenomics to map the diverse and previously unknown bacteria responsible for taking up methane across Denmark’s varied environments and highlight the natural habitats and methanotroph species with the potential for methane mitigation.
